decisions.reason: The signal-connector change does not alter the interboard power interface; the same message's separate power-input specification is already represented by the candidate's existing MODIFY.
The candidate's existing message-371 MODIFY already includes the complete six-pin main-board signal input and its pinout, so no additional or corrected Event is needed.
Identifying SDA0, SCL0, SDA1, and SCL1 on the connector does not change cable length, bus speed, pull-ups, or series-resistor conditioning.
The source specifies logical signal names on an interboard connector but does not assign or change any ESP32-S3 GPIO numbers.
The main-to-sensor connector carries I2C and UART signals and does not change the native USB D+ and D- programming interface.
The sensor-board signal connector specification does not affect the separate charge-status LED path, connector, or resistor configuration.
The SPS30 SEL-to-GND I2C-mode decision is already represented by its message-371 INTRODUCE and is not an omitted consequence of the interboard signal-interface MODIFY.
The battery connector is a separate power-board interface and is unaffected by the main-to-sensor signal connector type, pitch, pin count, or pinout.
The panel reset connector and EN-to-GND action are independent of the sensor-board interboard signal connector.
The panel button and switch connectors and GPIO assignments remain unchanged by the sensor-board signal-interface specification.
The PIR connector requirement is not changed by the separate main-to-sensor I2C and UART signal connector.
The source changes an electrical connector on the main-to-sensor link and does not alter the power board's dimensions, orientation, mounting, spacing, or connector placement.
